newsitem.title: DENMARK: ISS weighing sale of U.K. supply unit.
newsitem.headline: ISS weighing sale of U.K. supply unit.

text.p: Danish cleaning group International Service System (ISS) said on Tuesday it was considering the sale its British supply house ISS Darenas Ltd (U.K.) by the end of the year.
Last month, the group sold ISS Darenas International, which supplies cleaning materials and equipment to ISS companies and other clients in Scandinavia, to the Unilever group.
"ISS has been approached by several parties interested in acquiring ISS Darenas Ltd (U.K.)," ISS wrote in a statement accompanying its first-half results.

"If satisfactory terms can be obtained it is possible that ISS Darenas Ltd (U.K.) will be divested by the end of the year, thus increasing ISS Europe's ability to grow by selected acquisitions," it added.
It did not name prospective buyers.
The company said that income from the sale of ISS Darenas International would contribute a "substantial gain" to its second-half 1997 results.

The group, which was hit heavily last year by falsified accounting in U.S. unit ISS Inc, reported first half 1997 net profit of 83 million crowns compared to a loss of 2.02 billion in the first six months of 1996.
